title: set refuses an item as its own discovery source
findings_note: s369 relay review 2026-10-19: `set S01 --discovered-from S01` is accepted; `add` cannot create a self reference, and one makes `remove --purge` need `--force` and keeps the id from being reclaimed
boundary: **Not in this slice:** how `remove --purge` or id reclaim treat `discovered_from` references from other items.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
s369 gave `set` a `--discovered-from` flag with the same check as `add`: an empty value clears it, and any other value must exist. `add` cannot name the item it is filing, so the check never had to refuse a self reference. `set` can. An item that names itself is listed as its own blocker by `remove --purge` (`ops.py` removal reasons, "discovered from it") and by `_reclaim_check`, so it needs `--force` and burns its id. `--parent` already refuses this case as `parent_self` (`_check_parent` in `src/slicer/ops.py`).

Two smaller notes from the same review ride along. The `field_in_promote_source` row in `docs/agents.md` still says those fields "belong on `add`/`set`", while the message now names the exact `set` flag. No test covers `set --discovered-from` across several ids or a batch that names an unknown source; the reviewer checked both by hand.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/ops.py` (`set_fields_many`, next to the `discovered_from` require check).
- `tests/test_ops.py` (next to `test_Set_DiscoveredFrom_SetsAndClears`).
- `docs/commands.md` (the `set` row and Discovery provenance), `docs/agents.md` (the `field_in_promote_source` row and, if a code is added, the error-code table), `CHANGELOG.md` under Changed.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `test_Set_DiscoveredFromSelf_RefusesAndWritesNothing`: `set S01 --discovered-from S01` exits 2 with a self-reference code, and the index is unchanged.
- `test_Set_DiscoveredFromSeveralIds_SetsEach`: `set S02 S03 --discovered-from S01` sets both.
- `test_Set_DiscoveredFromUnknownInBatch_WritesNothing`: `set S02 S03 --discovered-from S99` refuses with `no_such_item`, and neither item changes.
- In a batch, an item that names itself (`set S01 S02 --discovered-from S01`) refuses the whole batch; cover it in the self test.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests; watch the self test go red. The two batch tests pin current behaviour, so mutation-check them instead.
2. Refuse when the source equals any id in the batch, before anything is written, with a code modelled on `parent_self` (proposed: `discovered_from_self`). The message says how to clear it (`set ID --discovered-from ''`).
3. Reword the `field_in_promote_source` row in `docs/agents.md` to say the message names the `set` flag that changes the field. Add the new code to the error-code table. Update `docs/commands.md` and CHANGELOG.
4. Mutation-check each new test.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - `python3.12 tests/affected.py --run`, then the full suite. `slicer check` passes.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch; the owner lands it.
